skill.name: writing-plans

content.value_statement: Complex coding work can stall when requirements are vague or tasks are too large. This skill turns a spec into a test-first implementation plan with files, commands, and handoff steps.
actual_capabilities: Creates a plan header with goal, architecture, and tech stack.
Breaks implementation work into small test-first tasks.
Names files to create, modify, and test.
Includes example test commands and expected outcomes.
Adds execution handoff options for follow-up work.
limitations: It does not inspect the repository unless the agent gathers context separately.
It does not execute the plan or verify code changes.
Example commands must be adapted to the project test runner.
It assumes a development workflow with tests and commits.

use_cases.title: Plan a new feature
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into a sequenced implementation plan with files, tests, and expected checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Prepare a refactor
use_cases.description: Break a risky code change into small tasks that preserve behavior and add focused tests.

use_cases.title: Hand off AI coding work
use_cases.description: Create a clear plan that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can follow in later implementation sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Feature Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you have a short feature request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill. Create an implementation plan for this feature: [paste requirements]. Include goal, files, tests, commands, and handoff options.

prompt_templates.title: Test-First Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when test coverage is important.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill. Build a test-first plan for [feature]. Separate failing tests, minimal implementation, passing checks, and commit steps.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill. Plan a refactor for [area]. Preserve current behavior, identify files, add regression tests, and list verification commands.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Task Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex work that may continue in another session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill. Create a detailed handoff plan for [project]. Include architecture notes, task sequence, review checkpoints, and execution options.

output_examples.input: Plan a password reset feature for an existing web app.
output_examples.output: A plan with a goal, architecture notes, file list, test-first tasks, verification commands, and execution handoff choices.

output_examples.input: Plan a refactor of billing validation without changing behavior.
output_examples.output: A task sequence covering regression tests, small code changes, expected test results, documentation updates, and commit points.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff plan for adding project export support.
output_examples.output: A saved implementation plan with scoped tasks, exact files to inspect, test expectations, and next-session execution guidance.

best_practices: Provide the feature requirements and any known technical constraints before asking for the plan.
Ask the agent to inspect relevant files before finalizing exact file paths.
Review generated commands and expected outputs against your project tooling.
anti_patterns: Do not use the plan as a substitute for repository context.
Do not accept vague tasks that lack files, tests, or verification steps.
Do not run example commands without checking paths and test names first.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a structured implementation plan with goals, architecture notes, file targets, test steps, commands, and handoff options.

faq.question: Does it write or modify code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is for planning before code changes begin.

faq.question: Can it support test-driven development?
faq.answer: Yes. Its task format starts with failing tests, then minimal implementation, verification, and commit steps.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require a specific project structure?
faq.answer: No. The generated plan should adapt file paths, tests, and commands to the current project.

faq.question: Is it safe to install?
faq.answer: The skill contains Markdown instructions and examples. The reported command findings are not executable code.
